ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a vertical wire/left power rail, marked with point T; on the right side is a vertical wire/right power rail, marked with point P. Above, there is a horizontal branch connected from the left rail to the right rail, with three resistors of the same shape connected in series on the branch, and the nodes after the first and second resistors are respectively marked W and U. In the middle, there is also a horizontal branch likewise connected from the left rail to the right rail, with three resistors of the same shape also connected in series on the branch, and the nodes after the first and second resistors are respectively marked S and Q. The bottom battery is connected between the left and right rails. Reasoning: The problem states that all resistance values are the same, and the voltmeter resistance is very large, so when the voltmeter is connected, it takes almost no current and does not change the potential distribution of the original circuit. The upper and middle two branches are both connected in parallel between the same pair of endpoints T and P, and each branch is three identical resistors connected in series, so each branch is the same voltage divider that divides the voltage into three equal parts. Starting from the left rail, the node after passing through two identical resistors is at the same voltage-division position in the two branches. This node on the upper branch is U, and this node on the middle branch is Q, so U and Q have the same potential. When the voltmeter is connected between two points with the same potential, the reading is zero.

raw_record.question_text: In the circuit shown below, each of the resistors has the same resistance. A voltmeter with very high resistance is connected between two points in the circuit. Between which two points of connection would the voltmeter read zero?

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as two horizontal resistor strings connected in parallel between the same left rail T and right rail P. The top string has three equal resistors with W after the first and U after the second; the middle string has three equal resistors with S after the first and Q after the second. Read from the text that all resistors have the same resistance and that the voltmeter has very high resistance, so it draws negligible current. Treat each string as a 3-resistor voltage divider across the same two rail potentials. In either string, the node after two equal resistors from the left rail is at the same fraction of the total rail-to-rail voltage. Therefore U on the top branch and Q on the middle branch are at the same potential, so a voltmeter between Q and U reads zero.
